Lines m and n are cut by transversal t, and a pair of alternate interior angles is congruent. Explain why m and n must be parallel. (Suppose they meet at a point P, and look at the triangle formed with t.)
required_method: A complete argument: if m and n met at P, they would form a triangle with t. One of the congruent angles would be an exterior angle of that triangle and the other a remote interior angle. But an exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles, so it is greater than either one. That is a contradiction, so m and n do not meet: they are parallel.

question: Lines a and b are cut by a transversal. A pair of corresponding angles measure (4x + 6)° and (5x - 9)°. For what value of x are the lines parallel?

choices: A. A pair of alternate interior angles | B. A pair of vertical angles | C. A linear pair | D. Two adjacent angles on the same line
correct_answer: A pair of alternate interior angles

question: If the same-side interior angles formed by a transversal add to 180°, the two lines are parallel.
If the vertical angles at one intersection are congruent, the two lines cut by the transversal are parallel.

question: Use a compass and straightedge to construct the line through P that is parallel to line k. Draw a transversal through P, then copy the angle it makes with k so that it is a corresponding angle at P. Leave your construction marks.
correct_answer: A transversal through P and k, the arcs used to copy the angle at P, and a line through P parallel to k. Any correct compass-and-straightedge construction with visible marks is accepted.

question: Why does copying the angle in that construction give a line that is parallel to k?
correct_answer: The copied angle and the angle at k are congruent corresponding angles, so the lines are parallel.

question: When a parallel line is constructed by copying an angle, which angles are made congruent?
choices: A. Vertical angles | B. Corresponding angles formed by the transversal | C. A linear pair | D. Two angles of a triangle
correct_answer: Corresponding angles formed by the transversal

question: Triangle ABC has angles of 35° and 85°. Triangle DEF has angles of 35° and 60°. Are the triangles similar? Explain.
correct_answer: Yes. The third angle of DEF is 180° - 35° - 60° = 85°, so two pairs of angles are equal (AA).

question: A 5-foot post casts a 3-foot shadow. At the same time, a tree casts a 12-foot shadow. Explain why the two triangles are similar, and find the height of the tree.
correct_answer: Both triangles have a right angle and the same angle of the sun's rays, so they are similar by AA. The tree is 20 feet tall.
grading_note: Grade both: the AA reason and 20 feet.

question: Which information shows that two triangles are similar by the angle-angle criterion?
choices: A. One pair of sides is proportional. | B. All the sides are equal. | C. Two pairs of corresponding angles are equal. | D. One pair of corresponding angles is equal.
correct_answer: Two pairs of corresponding angles are equal.

question: In the figure, segment DE is parallel to BC. Explain why triangle ADE is similar to triangle ABC.
correct_answer: The triangles share angle A, and angle ADE = angle ABC (corresponding angles, because DE ∥ BC). So they are similar by AA.

A triangle must have angles of 30°, 60°, and 90°. Do these conditions determine one triangle, more than one triangle, or no triangle?

question: Triangles ABC and DEF have angle A = angle D and angle B = angle E. Which transformations show that the triangles are similar?
correct_answer: A dilation that makes AB the same length as DE, followed by rigid motions that move the image onto DEF; the equal angles make the third vertices match.

question: Triangles ABC and DEF have angle A = angle D and angle B = angle E. Explain why a similarity transformation maps triangle ABC onto triangle DEF.
correct_answer: Dilate ABC by the scale factor DE ÷ AB, so the image of AB has the same length as DE. Rigid motions then move that image onto DE (A onto D, B onto E), with the third vertex on the same side as F. Because angle A = angle D and angle B = angle E, the image's other two sides lie along rays DF and EF, and two rays meet in only one point, so the third vertex lands on F. (The third angles are then equal too.)
grading_note: Full credit needs the dilation, the rigid motions, and why the third vertex must land on F.

question: Triangles with angles 30°, 70°, 80° and 70°, 30°, 80° are...
choices: A. congruent in every case | B. similar | C. not similar | D. impossible to compare

Two isosceles triangles are always similar.

correct_answer: CD = 6. Triangles ACD and CBD are similar, so AD ÷ CD = CD ÷ DB and CD² = 4 · 9 = 36.
grading_note: Both the length and the similar triangles are required.

In right triangle ABC with the right angle at C, and D the foot of the altitude from C to hypotenuse AB, AC² = AD · DB.
grading_note: AC² = AD · AB; it is CD² that equals AD · DB.

question: Triangle ABC has angles of 40° at A and 75° at B. Triangle DEF has angles of 40° at D and 75° at E, and DE = 2 · AB. Explain, using a dilation and rigid motions, why the triangles are similar.
required_method: Dilate ABC by a scale factor of 2, so the image of AB has the same length as DE. Rigid motions then move that image onto DE, with the third vertex on the same side as F. The 40° and 75° angles make the other two sides lie along rays DF and EF, which meet at only one point, so the third vertex lands on F. A dilation followed by rigid motions maps ABC onto DEF.

question: Explain why two triangles with two pairs of equal angles must also have the third pair of angles equal.
required_method: In each triangle the three angles add to 180°, so each third angle equals 180° minus the same two measures. The third angles are equal.

question: Use a ruler and a protractor to draw two triangles of different sizes that each have angles of 50° and 60°. Measure their sides, and compare the ratios of corresponding sides.
correct_answer: The ratios of corresponding sides are all about the same (equal up to measuring error), so the triangles are similar.

grading_note: Grade the two drawings and the ratios computed from the student's own measurements; there is no preset size.

question: Which argument shows that two triangles with two pairs of equal angles are similar?
choices: A. Rotate one triangle 90°. | B. Dilate one so a pair of corresponding sides match, then use rigid motions; the equal angles force the third vertices to match. | C. Check that the triangles have equal areas. | D. Measure all three sides of each and check that they are equal.
correct_answer: Dilate one so a pair of corresponding sides match, then use rigid motions; the equal angles force the third vertices to match.

question: The figure shows a square with sides a + b, made of four right triangles and a tilted square with side c. Explain how the figure proves that a² + b² = c².
required_method: A complete argument: the large square's area is (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²; it is also 4 triangles (4 · {1/2}ab = 2ab) plus the inner square c²; so a² + 2ab + b² = 2ab + c², and subtracting 2ab gives a² + b² = c². Any equivalent wording is accepted.
